strengths: Well-motivated problem with rigorous motivational study (Section 2.2) demonstrating clear limitations of existing T2I methods through concrete examples
Practical modular design using lightweight adapter to avoid retraining frozen diffusion backbones, enabling efficient cross-domain transfer
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse domains (synthetic, facial, medical) with multiple complementary metrics (effectiveness, composition, realism, minimality)
Strong empirical results: 91% MAE reduction on Pendulum, 86% LPIPS on CelebA, 87% FID on ADNI; competitive or superior to baselines
Thoughtful technical design: Prompt-Aligned Injection creatively maps scalar attributes to learned token embeddings to address numeric-spatial alignment
Thorough ablation studies quantifying contribution of PAI and CTC regularizers
Good reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameters, algorithm descriptions, and promised code release
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging evaluation failures in OOD settings with concrete examples
weaknesses: Incomplete comparison with recent diffusion-based baselines: Main results omit DiffSCM, Pan & Bareinboim 2024, and Rasal et al. 2025; only CausalDiffAE and DisDiffAE included for Pendulum/CelebA, undermining 'state-of-the-art' claims
Strong unexamined assumption of known causal graphs G—no robustness analysis of graph misspecification; severely limits real-world applicability where causal structures are typically unknown

Limited theoretical justification for regularization strategies: Why PAI solves alignment and why CTC's inter/intra-token separation achieves causal disentanglement are asserted rather than formally justified; no theoretical guarantees
Causal mechanism identifiability not discussed: MLE fitting (Eq. 3) requires unstated assumptions; additive noise model (Eq. 2) may be too restrictive for complex causal relationships

Evaluation relies entirely on classifiers: No human evaluation for subjective quality; pre-trained classifiers have known biases and OOD failure modes; CLD metric validity (unconditional VAE latent distance) is questionable for semantic minimality
No cross-domain generalization testing: All experiments train and test within same domain, limiting evidence of robustness

Limited conceptual novelty: Individual components established (adapter-based guidance, contrastive disentanglement, SCM counterfactuals); contribution is primarily in combination/application rather than new methodology or theoretical insights
Hyperparameter sensitivity under-explored: Guidance scale α, CTC temperature τ, and scaling λ lack principled selection strategies; Table 6 shows α sensitivity but no guidance on selection
Attention Guidance appears orthogonal to core method: Sometimes degrades performance (Table 8), suggesting method robustness issues; feels like post-hoc technique rather than core contribution

Missing implementation details: How are attributes Y extracted/labeled for ADNI? Which validation set for hyperparameter tuning? No discussion of label quality assurance or sensitivity to annotation accuracy

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear limitations of existing methods demonstrated through convincing examples (Section 2.2, Appendix B)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse datasets (Pendulum, CelebA, ADNI) with multiple metrics following established benchmarking protocols
Practical modular architecture that doesn't require retraining the entire diffusion backbone
Extensive ablation studies and thorough supplementary materials supporting reproducibility
Honest discussion of limitations, particularly the OOD evaluation failure case in Appendix F
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: causal mechanisms use standard additive noise models, adapter architecture directly builds on prior work (Zhang et al. 2023, Mou et al. 2024), PAI is straightforward learnable embeddings, and CTC is direct application of InfoNCE contrastive loss
Unrealistic assumption of pre-specified causal graphs; no structure learning or learning methods; graphs assumed correct without validation, making the approach difficult to apply in practice

Significant evaluation limitations: no human evaluation; reliance on classifier-based metrics that fail in OOD cases (acknowledged in Fig. 26 with bearded females example); missing comparisons with recent counterfactual-specific methods (Rasal et al. 2025, Pan & Bareinboim 2024, Xia et al. 2025) on CelebA/ADNI

Methodological clarity issues: the connection between semantic attributes and diffusion latents is underexplained; why text embedding injection works better than direct injection lacks principled justification; ambiguity on whether causal mechanisms and adapter are trained jointly or sequentially

Mixed empirical results: beard F1 of 51.9 on CelebA (Table 2) is weak; improvements over baselines are inconsistent across metrics; gain from PAI (+11.6% avg) is modest given added complexity; CTC provides marginal improvements

Generalization concerns: only tested on simple structures with 4-6 attributes; requires annotated attributes for training; medical imaging claims (ADNI) lack clinical validation despite claiming breakthrough results; no analysis of transfer to new domains
Missing ablations: no separate study of causal mechanism learning; no investigation of mechanism parameterization alternatives; limited analysis of what PAI and CTC actually learn representationally

Incomplete baseline comparisons: recent counterfactual methods (Rasal et al., Pan & Bareinboim, Xia et al.) cited but not compared on main datasets; only compared against outdated baselines (VAE 2013, GAN 2014) not designed for counterfactual generation
No human evaluation on arguably the most important dimension—whether counterfactuals are actually faithful and realistic to human judges
Attention guidance component appears orthogonal and unprincipled; results differ significantly with/without AG (Table 8), suggesting methodological instability

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem with compelling empirical demonstration of limitations of existing T2I methods for counterfactual generation
Sound technical approach integrating SCMs with diffusion adapters; elegant solution avoiding costly retraining of frozen backbones
Novel combination of Prompt-Aligned Injection (PAI) and Conditioned Token Contrastive Loss (CTC) for semantic-spatial alignment and disentanglement
Comprehensive cross-domain experimental validation (Pendulum, CelebA, ADNI) with strong empirical results (91% MAE reduction, 86% LPIPS reduction, 87% FID reduction)
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component (+11.6% F1 with PAI, additional gains with CTC)
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, effective visualizations, and well-structured methodology
Exceptional reproducibility: detailed implementation details, all hyperparameters specified, promise to release code, public datasets used
Honest discussion of limitations (Appendix F) including OOD evaluation issues and fairness considerations; ethics statement provided
weaknesses: Strong assumptions (known causal graph, Markovian SCMs, known attributes at training time) significantly limit applicability; no sensitivity analysis to graph misspecification
Somewhat incremental contribution—primarily engineering-focused combination of existing techniques (adapters, SCMs, contrastive learning) rather than fundamentally novel ideas

Incomplete experimental comparisons: CausalDiffAE only shown on Pendulum; recent work (Rasal et al. 2025, Xia et al. 2025) not experimentally compared on same benchmarks; limited to older baselines (VAE/HVAE/GAN) on CelebA/ADNI

Limited theoretical justification for design choices: PAI via text embeddings vs. alternatives (only empirical evidence); temperature τ=0.2 and λ=0.0005 appear ad-hoc; connection between attention map quality and causal faithfulness unclear

Serious evaluation metric limitations: acknowledged OOD classifier bias (e.g., bearded females misclassified as male) undermines evaluation validity; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; pretrained classifiers introduce circular evaluation risk

Limited evaluation scope: all experiments on simple, structured domains with 4-6 variables; unclear scalability to complex causal structures; no testing on truly OOD domains or high-dimensional attribute spaces
Dependence on DDIM inversion robustness not analyzed; method relies on accurate abduction step but inversion errors and their propagation unexplored
Attention Guidance (AG) shows unexpected fragility (F1 drops from 38.2 to 28.1 for plain adapter) and appears to require prior regularization; suggests method may be brittle without both PAI and CTC

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear demonstration of limitations of existing T2I methods through systematic motivational study
Practical modular design that works with frozen diffusion models across multiple architectures (SD1.5, DiT, SD3) without retraining
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse datasets (Pendulum, CelebA, ADNI) with systematic evaluation on four complementary metrics and multiple baselines
Thorough ablation studies clearly demonstrating the necessity and contribution of proposed regularization techniques (PAI: +11.6% F1, CTC: improved disentanglement)
Strong quantitative results with significant improvements: 91% MAE reduction on Pendulum, 87% FID reduction on ADNI, 86% LPIPS reduction on CelebA
Extensive supplementary material with detailed implementation, additional experiments (causal discovery, stress tests, generalization to SD3), and careful treatment of assumptions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (adapter architecture, PAI mechanism, CTC loss) are straightforward applications of existing techniques; main contribution is their combination with SCM, which is incremental

Strong assumption of known causal graph significantly limits practical applicability; robustness to graph misspecification not thoroughly analyzed; assumption acknowledged but not adequately addressed in limitations
Counterfactual identifiability not formally guaranteed due to approximate DDIM inversion; the method cannot ensure recovery of true exogenous noise, undermining causal validity claims

Weak theoretical justification for why proposed regularization strategies work: no principled explanation for PAI-induced disentanglement or theoretical analysis of CTC's effectiveness on token separation

Evaluation lacks human studies critical for assessing visual quality and counterfactual faithfulness; reliance on pretrained classifiers for effectiveness metrics introduces potential bias; FID and CLD metrics computed in proxy spaces that may not reflect true causal relationships
Limited failure analysis: all presented results appear successful with no discussion of failure modes, edge cases with complex attribute interactions, or performance degradation scenarios

Incomplete comparisons: motivational study compares with general editing methods (NTI, MCPL) rather than counterfactual approaches; DiffCounter comparison limited to CelebA-HQ; some recent counterfactual methods not included

Computational efficiency not discussed: inference time not compared to baselines; training time and parameter overhead not analyzed; hyperparameter choices (λ=0.0005, τ=0.2) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

strengths: Well-motivated problem with effective demonstation of existing T2I method limitations through systematic experiments
Practical modular design that preserves frozen backbone and generalizes across diffusion architectures (SD1.5, SD3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse datasets with multiple metrics and extensive ablations
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of method and results
weaknesses: Core causal validity claim is unsupported: DDIM inversion is approximate and no formal guarantees provided; causal graph must be known and correct without sensitivity analysis for misspecification; evaluation using anti-causal predictors cannot assess true causal faithfulness

Limited technical novelty: adapter architecture from controllable diffusion literature; PAI similar to Textual Inversion/MCPL; CTC is standard InfoNCE loss; contribution is primarily combining existing components

Evaluation methodology fundamentally flawed: using classifiers trained on observational data to evaluate counterfactuals conflates 'looks correct' with 'causally correct' and cannot detect violations; inconsistent results (Age F1 worse than HVAE); FID improvements don't guarantee causal faithfulness

Restrictive causal model (Eq. 1): linear form with additive Gaussian noise cannot capture nonlinear relationships; assumption choices (linearity, Gaussian noise) unjustified; no validation that learned mechanisms respect causal graph

Strong unjustified assumptions: requires known correct causal graph with no analysis of misspecification sensitivity; structure learning relegated to preliminary appendix; predefined graph limits real-world applicability
Limited scope: simple discrete attributes and relatively straightforward continuous attributes; no complex causal structures (hidden confounders, nonlinearity, cycles); scalability unclear

Missing causal validation: no experiments validating graph-respecting counterfactuals; no quantitative disentanglement metrics; cross-attention visualizations only qualitative; no user studies for identity preservation claims
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned; heavy appendix reliance; implementation details unclear; hyperparameter choices lack justification
Medical applications (ADNI) insufficient ethical discussion despite high-stakes consequences if counterfactuals unfaithful; dismissive boilerplate impact statement

strengths: Well-motivated problem analysis with convincing motivational studies demonstrating concrete limitations of prior prompt-based and diffusion+SCM approaches
Elegant solution design that keeps backbone frozen while adding compact modular adapter, enabling broad applicability across different T2I backbones (SD1.5, SD3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse datasets (Pendulum, CelebA, ADNI, CelebA-HQ) with multiple evaluation metrics (effectiveness, composition, realism, minimality)
Strong empirical results with 91% MAE reduction on Pendulum, 79-87% FID reduction, and 86% LPIPS improvement on CelebA, consistently outperforming baselines
Extensive ablation studies investigating guidance scales, DDIM steps, and regularizer contributions, with proper benchmarking protocol and non-cherry-picked results
Technically sound implementation of Pearl's abduction-action-prediction framework with interpretable SCM formulation
Exceptional supplementary material (47 pages) including causal discovery extension, detailed implementation, attention visualizations, and learning dynamics
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—combines existing techniques (adapters from controllable diffusion, PAI via simple projection, standard InfoNCE loss) without introducing fundamentally new components

Strong restrictive assumption of known causal graph severely limits practical applicability; causal discovery extension (Appendix G) shows competitive but not superior results compared to SDCD/NOTEARS

Unresolved counterfactual identifiability concerns—relies on DDIM inversion to recover exogenous noise without formal guarantees; Appendix F provides only empirical reversibility evidence, not theoretical identifiability

Incomplete justification of design choices: why PAI enables semantic-spatial alignment lacks rigorous analysis; hyperparameters (λ=0.0005, τ=0.2) appear arbitrary without ablation; linear projection gi(yi) not validated against alternatives

Evaluation limitations: effectiveness depends on pre-trained classifier quality without bias analysis; CLD metric relies on VAE introducing additional bias; no human perceptual studies; modest improvements over recent baseline (DiffCounter) suggest gains diminish on stronger baselines
No systematic failure analysis or investigation of challenging cases; missing discussion of robustness to graph misspecification or performance on out-of-distribution images

Incomplete theoretical understanding: how residual injection affects diffusion dynamics mathematically unclear; optimization landscape and convergence properties not analyzed; connection between equation (1) and diffusion process lacks rigor
Limited generalization analysis: only face and medical domains; no domain adaptation studies or evaluation on other image categories
